A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAMEOPT research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments on four protein datasets, including simulations using learned fitness oracles, baseline comparisons, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds sensitivity studies, acquisition-function analyses, and comparisons with latent-space optimizers.

M1.justification: The principal UCB-based algorithm and equilibrium-finding subroutines remain unchanged. Appendices E.11–E.12 instantiate additional variants using expected improvement as the game reward and an RBF/string structure-coupled surrogate kernel, representing limited component substitutions.

E1.justification: Both versions use GB1(4), GB1(55), Halogenase, and GFP for the same protein-fitness objectives. The new unequal-action experiments regroup existing protein sites without changing the represented sequences or task; other additions vary experimental configurations.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparison methods through GP-EI in Figure 16 and latent-space optimizers in Figure 17: Naïve LSBO with RBF and LADDER with the structure-coupled kernel. The original GP-UCB, IBR-FITNESS, PR, RANDOM, and discrete-local-search comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols test batch sizes 1, 3, 10, and 50 alongside the retained size 5, unequal player groupings, learning-rate sweeps, and alternative acquisition functions and kernels. Table 1 also replaces fixed domain-specific learning rates with a tuning grid; this reported revision does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's initialization, diversity, and equal-size grouping analyses, v2 adds unequal-grouping robustness, batch-size sensitivity, HEDGE learning-rate and game-convergence checks, sampled-UCB analysis, and acquisition-function/kernel sensitivity studies in E.7–E.12.

E5.justification: The original 18- or 10-replication reporting, interquartile-range plots, and runtime standard deviations are retained. The additions introduce no documented change in uncertainty-estimation practice, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Original results in Figures 2–10 and Tables 2–6 remain unchanged. Figures 11–17 add outcomes for unequal groupings, batch sizes, learning rates, UCB trajectories, EI, and latent-space comparisons. These are newly reported results under additional configurations, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the GP posterior expression's conditioning variable from f_t to the noisy observations Y_t. The equilibrium definitions, sample-complexity theorem, convergence rate, and complete Appendix A proof otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: tractable combinatorial BO through optimistic game equilibria, approximate-equilibrium sample complexity, and effective protein optimization. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 and the new appendices clarify acquisition-optimization efficiency, discuss applicability across configurations, and attribute weak latent-space results to decoder dependence. These extend the interpretation while retaining the earlier explanation based on exploration and local equilibria.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access pointer and describes the new latent optimizers' transformer decoder, ESM-1v embeddings, and beam search. Hyperparameter documentation changes, but its learning-rate grid is inconsistent: Table 1 includes 0.9, whereas Figure 14 shows 2.5 instead.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 and E.12 add substantive positioning against latent-space BO, distinguishing direct sequence optimization from methods requiring decoding. New coverage includes Gómez-Bombarelli, Deshwal and Doppa, Tripp, and Maus, alongside added references concerning GP-based games, EI, and string kernels.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local notation clarifications, an expanded Section 5.5 with topical paragraphs, moving the GP-UCB appendix discussion from E.5 to E.2, adding acknowledgements, and removing the societal-impact paragraph.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven multi-panel figures covering the new analyses; Figure 13 also redisplays existing batch-size-5 panels. Existing graphics are retained and redistributed, tables are restyled, and the document adopts ICLR headers and title formatting.

improvement.justification: v2 gives direct empirical support for v1's asserted flexibility beyond batch size 5 and UCB, adds useful convergence checks and alternative comparators, and supplies a code pointer. These strengthen an already substantial experimental study. The gains remain bounded by sparse decoder-comparison details and inconsistent learning-rate documentation between Table 1 and Figure 14.
